newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Gle des Eaux finalising team for Manila water bid.
newsitem.headline: Gle des Eaux finalising team for Manila water bid.

text.p: Compagnie Generale des Eaux (CGE) will finalise this week the composition of a consortium it is leading that will bid for the privatisation of the Philippines' largest water utility, a CGE oficial said on Monday.

"We will finalise by Friday the last local company that will be part of the consortium," said Jean-Marie Messier, chairman and chief executive officer of CGE, which is leading one of the groups bidding to privatise the Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System (MWSS).
He declined to disclose the name of the company.
Messier said CGE and leading local partner Aboitiz Equity Ventures hold more than 50 percent stake in the consortium dubbed the Pilipinas Water Corporation.
Other members of the consortium are Marubeni Corp, Dharmala Philippines Inc, Puncak Niaga Sdn Berhad and House of Investments Inc.
The bidding for two 25-year service contracts for MWSS has been scheduled for the end of the year, with the final contracts to be awarded in January.
Messier said the CGE-led consortium will comply with the 60-40 percent ownership requirement of Philippine laws under which 60 percent of a joint venture should be owned by Filipinos.
CGE is one of four interested groups that the MWSS has shortlisted for its privatisation.
"We are confident that the expertise of the consortium will allow us to be the cheapest bidder not only for Day One but for the rest of the 25 years," Messier added.
He said that only 66 percent of Manila residents have access to a water network and 55 percent of the water supply is lost through leaks and defective meters.
